1stēlla: long e (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). The house spelling.

stēlla1, stēllae f.

noun, first declension

The house spelling.

Other words

  • sīdus, sīderis n. — star, constellation

    noun, third declension · also used · classical

  • astrum, astrī n. — a star, a constellation

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. E. 9.47 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Tusc. 1.62 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov., Hor.)

Examples

  • Quot stēllae in caelō sunt? — Innumerābilēs.

    How many stars are in the sky? — Too many to count.composed

  • macte novā virtūte, puer, sīc ītur ad astra

    a blessing on your new-found courage, boy: that is the way to the starsVerg. A. 9.641

See also moon, starfish.
